# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Keeper of the Four Winds Point lighthouse, former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is a tall, ungainly, and stooped old sailor suggestive of great strength and endurance, though he appears frail and bent in his final spring. He has a clean-shaven, deeply lined, and bronzed face, and a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders. His deep-set blue eyes are remarkably bright, sometimes twinkling or dreaming, and often gazing seaward with a wistful quest.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c30 P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 c30 P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a high-souled, simple-minded, and cheerful man possessing eternal youth in his heart and eyes. A passionate worshipper of beauty, he finds subtle joy in every lovely sight or sound. He is placid and virtually impossible to anger, preferring to defend others against unproven accusations. Marked by a chronic habit of enjoying life and a deep mixture of kindness and wisdom, he embraces both joyous and disagreeable things with humor and philosophical grace.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), [v4 c22 P13](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0013)_

## History

Captain Jim spent his childhood in Four Winds, befriending local schoolmaster John Selwyn at age sixteen. Coming from a line of seafarers, he ran off to sea as a boy and spent the next six decades traveling all over the world. Over fifty years ago, he lost his sweetheart Margaret when her dory drifted out to sea during a sudden storm. After searching the shoreline in vain for months, he carried her memory with him through all his voyages. Five years before meeting Anne Blythe, he gave up seafaring and became the keeper of the Four Winds Point lighthouse. During his travels, he discovered an amnesiac, injured Dick Moore in Cuba and brought him home to Leslie Moore. He rescued a abandoned cat, naming him the First Mate, and regularly visited Anne and Gilbert Blythe, forming a close bond with them as kindred spirits. Together with author Owen Ford, he collaborated to publish his life's experiences in a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim. After seeing the publication of his life-book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully.

_Sources: [v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015), [v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Descended from a family of sea-going folk  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Ran off to sea as a young boy and spent his life sailing the globe until retiring five years prior  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- Lost his sweetheart Margaret at sea over fifty years earlier and spent months searching the shore for her body  <sub>[v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017)</sub>

## Quotes

> You’re young and I’m old, but our souls are about the same age, I reckon.  <sub>[v4 c7 P54](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0054)</sub>

> I saved his life, and when you’ve saved a creature’s life you’re bound to love it. It’s next thing to giving life.  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>

> I’ve kind of contracted a habit of enj’ying things. It’s got so chronic that I believe I even enj’y the disagreeable things.  <sub>[v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)</sub>

> The sea took her from me, but some day I’ll find her. Mistress Blythe. It can’t keep us apart forever.  <sub>[v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017)</sub>

> A man can’t pick his time for dying, Mistress Blythe—jest got to go when the Great Captain gives His sailing orders.  <sub>[v4 c35 P34](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0034)</sub>
